sections.heading: Before you drive — C2
sections.markdown:
FACT_ID: sec01-R01 | anchor: A11
Start the turn signal at least one hundred feet before changing direction. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R02 | anchor: A11
Hazard lights help others see a vehicle that has stopped on the roadway or nearby. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R03 | anchor: A11
Sit upright with your back supported by the seat and your feet on the floor. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R04 | anchor: A11
Before moving, position the seat for a clear windshield view, full pedal and steering control, and enough room for air-bag deployment. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R05 | anchor: A12
A properly positioned seat lets your foot pivot easily between brake and accelerator while your heel stays on the floor. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R06 | anchor: A12
With the seat correctly adjusted, the steering-wheel top is no higher than your shoulders and remains below your chin. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R07 | anchor: A12
Keep at least ten inches between your chest and the steering wheel to provide space for air-bag deployment. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R08 | anchor: A12
Position the head restraint against the back of your head, at least as high as your ears, to help prevent whiplash. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R09 | anchor: A12
Set the mirrors before driving so they provide the best available view beside and behind the vehicle. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R10 | anchor: A12
Aim the interior rear-view mirror to frame the rear window and show traffic behind you. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R11 | anchor: A12
For the left outside mirror, rest your head against the closed driver-side window and adjust until only a small part of the vehicle's left edge remains visible. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R12 | anchor: A13
For the right outside mirror, lean until your head is over the center console, then adjust until the rear edge of your vehicle is barely visible. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R13 | anchor: A13
The described outside-mirror adjustment adds twelve to sixteen degrees of view on each side, although the vehicle's sides are no longer visible in a normal mirror glance. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R14 | anchor: A13
With the described mirror adjustment, a vehicle behind moves from the inside mirror to an outside mirror, then into the driver's peripheral view. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R15 | anchor: A13
Air bags supplement safety belts and work best together with them to reduce the chance of the head or upper body striking the interior in a crash. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R16 | anchor: A13
Consult the vehicle owner's manual for information specific to its air bags. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R17 | anchor: A13
Drivers and front-seat riders in most passenger vehicles must wear safety belts on Ohio roads, including vehicles equipped with air bags. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R18 | anchor: A13
Fasten your own safety belt and check that every passenger uses a safety belt or a child restraint. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R19 | anchor: A13
For a driver younger than eighteen, occupancy cannot exceed the number of originally installed safety belts, and every occupant must wear one. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R20 | anchor: A13
Place the safety belt over the body's bony shoulder and hip areas. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R21 | anchor: A13
Wear the shoulder belt over the shoulder and chest with little or no slack, never under an arm or behind the back. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R22 | anchor: A13
Incorrect shoulder-belt use can cause serious internal injury during a crash. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R23 | anchor: A13
After fastening, tighten the lap belt so it sits low and snug across the hips. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R24 | anchor: A13
A poorly positioned lap belt can let you slide out during a crash, causing injury or death. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

Confusables: service braking controls motion; parking braking holds a parked vehicle. Hazard lamps identify a stopped vehicle; turn signals communicate a planned change. Air bags supplement belts. Mnemonics: check, adjust, fasten. Glossary: tread is the tire surface measured in the cited tire checks; interior and outside mirrors have different viewing roles. These labels organize the cited facts and add no new driving rule.
